I need to ask about the nature of your abdominal pain and whether you have noticed any changes in your bowel habits or stool color. Can you also describe any skin rashes or itching you might be experiencing?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for describing the fixed, painless neck swelling; that is a significant finding. Given your systemic symptoms of fever, night sweats, weight loss, and lymphadenopathy, have you experienced any prolonged fevers or unexplained bleeding? Additionally, have you noticed any night sweats severe enough to soak your bedding?

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that update; the combination of an enlarged, fixed supraclavicular lymph node and abdominal fullness with your "B symptoms" (fever, night sweats, weight loss) is highly concerning for a malignancy. Given the fixed nature of the node and your symptoms, I am requesting a Computed Tomography (CT) scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis to visualize the extent of the disease.

REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest_Abdomen_Pelvis
REQUEST IMAGES: Lymph_Node_Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT Scan Thorax and Abdomen: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes; Lymph Node Ultrasound: Not provided in data.

text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lymphoma (likely Hodgkin Lymphoma or Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma)
